newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No chance N.Korea will turn to market-Moscow envoy.
newsitem.headline: No chance N.Korea will turn to market-Moscow envoy.

text.p: North Korea's envoy in Moscow said on Monday the very idea of his impoverished state accepting ideas of a market economy was "a fantasy", Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said.

"Any mention of market economy in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea is fantasy," Tass quoted ambassador Son Song-pil as saying during a meeting with radical leftist activists. "We will firmly pursue the policy worked out by Kim Il-sung."

The ambassador is a senior figure in the North Korean hierarchy. Moscow's ties to the Stalinist state have weakened since the collapse of the Soviet Union but Tass is still one of the few foreign media accredited by the Pyongyang authorities.

Commenting on the widely expected assumption of top state posts by Kim Jong-il, son of the late "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung, the ambassador said: "The whole of our people are impatiently waiting for this to happen, but so far there have been no decisions on when and how this will happen."
Since the death of his father on July 8, 1994, Kim Jong-il, now 55, has established full personal control but the formal top party post and the state presidency have been left vacant.
Earlier this month, the ambassador hinted that Kim Jong-il could be appointed supreme leader of the party and state after the end of the three-year official mourning for Kim Il-sung.
The mourning for the man who ruled his Stalinist state with an iron hand for more than four decades formally ended in July.
North Korea said on Friday that a heatwave and a subsequent drought were having a "catastrophic" impact on its economy and worsening food shortages there.

What it has called an "unprecedented" drought struck as it was struggling to survive widespread famine caused by floods that devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases in 1995 and 1996.
